name: How To Robot
shortDescription: Research pipeline that turns web video of people's hands into robot training data: 3D hand trajectories, retargeted to an arm, exported as LeRobot datasets.
description:
Teleoperation can't produce the volume of trajectories robot foundation models need, so How To Robot treats web video as the corpus instead. Give it a task ("how to pour tea"), and it finds clips, recovers 3D hand trajectories, re-expresses them relative to the object, retargets them onto a robot and exports LeRobot datasets and policies.

Highlights:
- Pipeline math tested end to end on toy data: hand pose to a 7-DOF task vector, atomic action segmentation (reach / grasp / manipulate / release), jitter augmentation, trajectory clustering and evaluation stats with a rollout logger.
- SO-101 retargeting and a MuJoCo sim environment, LeRobot dataset export, an ACT training script and closed-loop sim evaluation; the first toy ACT policy succeeds 10/10 in sim.
- Scoped as a research project: a feasibility review, research plan, open-questions log, an evaluation plan with three tasks and baselines, and a novel-view idea for synthesising robot-eye views from egocentric clips.
